title: Intro of a First Person maze game made in 4 days for Epic's AI Megajam:
author: PryTheSkyGames
selftext: You can check One Last Shot on Itch.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/PryTheSkyGames please share some more about how you used AI in developing this. Naming the tools or saying "made with AI" doesn't count. Rule 4 is how we keep promotional posts contributing, by having them talk about the process and how the game was made. Trying to keep the sub focused on dev. This post may be removed if it isn't updated.

replies.author: PryTheSkyGames
replies.body: I shared a comment and can share the detailed log here: [https://prytheskygames.itch.io/onelastshot/devlog/1781844/devlog](https://prytheskygames.itch.io/onelastshot/devlog/1781844/devlog)

comments.author: PryTheSkyGames
comments.body:
All the game was made with Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 on UE5. Except for a few key assets like some objects and costumes, all the assets are from the studios like Quixel, Dekogon and Befour. All the voice over and sounds are from Elevenlabs. Mocap was by a basic video shot with a phone and transferred to UE with Claude and I arranged the shots for this intro. You can ask anything about the process.

And here's the log:   
[https://prytheskygames.itch.io/onelastshot/devlog/1781844/devlog](https://prytheskygames.itch.io/onelastshot/devlog/1781844/devlog)

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: The players should be more observant and actively look around to assess their situation. They've just woken up in an unfamiliar area, so it would be natural for them to look around (especially behind them). And also acknowledge each other, with eye contact, because they are competing against each other after all. No one checked the protagonist after he stood up so it feels mechanical and less human.

replies.author: PryTheSkyGames
replies.body: Sure sure. But the jam is all about time management. So, I left things unfixed here and there in order to make a playable built ready. Even though I slept like 2 hours everyday in that process, it was really not easy to handle lots of things.
